name: Fusidic acid
executiveSummary: Steroid antibiotic (staphylococci). Topical skin: **2% cream/ointment q8–12h × 5–7 days**. Adult PO (fusidate): **500 mg q8h**. Ophthalmic: **drop q12h**. Not broad first-line systemic — resistance risk.
indications:
## Indications

- Localized staphylococcal skin infections (impetigo, folliculitis).
- Selected systemic staphylococcal infections (PO/IV) by susceptibility.
- Bacterial conjunctivitis (ophthalmic presentation).

## Precautions

- Hepatic: caution with prolonged PO (↑ bilirubin/enzymes).
- PO interactions: statins (myopathy), CYP3A4 inhibitors.
- Reserve systemic use; prefer topical for small lesions.

> Combinations with topical steroids: only short courses for infected eczema.

adulto.presentation: Cream/ointment 2%; tabs 250 mg (sodium fusidate); 1% eye drops.
adulto.dose: Skin: **q8–12h × 5–7 days** (usual max ~2 weeks). PO: **500 mg q8h** (severe: hospital regimens). Eye: **1 drop q12h** for several days after improvement.
adulto.notes: PO with food improves GI tolerance.

pediatrico.presentation: Cream 2%; suspension/tabs by country; eye drops.
pediatrico.dose: Topical: as adult. PO: often **20–40 mg/kg/day** divided q8h (adult max) — local label. Eye: **q12h**.
pediatrico.notes: In children prefer topical if limited infection.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Topical: local irritation. PO: nausea, diarrhea, jaundice/↑ enzymes; rare: skin reactions.
